context: Tests whether the agent audits the applicable readiness capabilities with evidence and gaps, separates repository and runner headlines from evidence strength, derives each headline from its lowest applicable owned capability, and produces a bounded init path that proves the app is ready.

checklist.name: Applicable readiness capabilities present
checklist.description: audit-report.md covers legibility, executability, feedback, safety, durability, and scale, marking genuinely inapplicable capabilities with a concrete reason

checklist.name: Capability grades used
checklist.description: Each applicable capability in audit-report.md receives an F-through-A grade, while N/A is used only with a concrete task-scope reason

checklist.name: Evidence cited per capability
checklist.description: Each capability in audit-report.md cites at least one specific file, exercised command, or observed runtime outcome as evidence

checklist.name: Gap described per capability
checklist.description: Each capability below the requested target includes the missing outcome and identifies whether the repository or runner owns it

checklist.name: Repository and runner grades use their lowest owned capability
checklist.description: audit-report.md reports separate repository and runner headline grades, each derived from its lowest applicable capability owned by that boundary rather than an average, and does not collapse them into one overall letter

checklist.name: Repository, runner, and evidence are separated
checklist.description: audit-report.md reports repository grade, runner grade, and E0-through-E4 evidence level separately instead of collapsing environment availability and proof strength into one letter

checklist.name: Background app start in init.sh
checklist.description: scripts/init.sh starts the application process in the background (using & or equivalent) so the script can poll

checklist.name: Bounded readiness wait in init.sh
checklist.description: scripts/init.sh polls health or another real readiness signal until a finite attempt or wall-clock deadline before declaring success

checklist.name: Non-zero exit on failure
checklist.description: scripts/init.sh exits with a non-zero status code (exit 1 or equivalent) if the app does not start successfully

checklist.name: Strict mode in init.sh
checklist.description: scripts/init.sh includes set -euo pipefail or equivalent strict mode at the top

checklist.name: Target progression is explicit
checklist.description: improvements.md or audit-report.md prioritizes cold start before real-surface feedback and repeated trials, identifies the remaining path toward B and A, and does not present reaching C as completion

checklist.name: No mock tests treated as real-surface proof
checklist.description: The report does not treat the mock-only Jest suite as passing testability or a substitute for real-process proof; it may still acknowledge isolated unit-level evidence
